chunks: And it was narrated from Abū Baṣīr that he said:

We stayed in a house in which there was a well, and beside it was a drain, with only about two arm-lengths between them. They refrained from performing wudu (ablution) from it, and that caused them hardship. So we entered upon Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام and informed him, and he said: “Perform wudu (ablution) from it, for that drain has channels that empty into a valley, which flows into the sea.”

key_terms.الْبَحْرِ: the sea, the final destination of the flowing drainage
key_terms.الْوُضُوءِ: wudu (ablution), the ritual washing before worship
key_terms.بَالُوعَةٌ: a drain or cesspit located near the well
key_terms.بِئْرٌ: a well from which water is drawn
key_terms.مَجَارِيَ: channels or conduits through which water flows
key_terms.وَادٍ: a valley into which the drainage empties

ai.seo_question: Can wudu (ablution) be performed from a well that is close to a drain?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about the permissibility of using water from a well located near a drain. Imam Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام clarifies that proximity alone does not make the water unsuitable for wudu (ablution), especially when the drain has an outlet flowing away.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.24 - It was narrated from Abu Basir that Imam (as) said:

"We stayed in a house with a well beside a drain, with only about two arm-lengths between them. The people refrained from performing ablution from it, which caused them difficulty. So we went to Abu Abdullah (as) and informed him.
Imam (as) said: 'Perform ablution from it, for that drain has channels that flow into a valley, which leads to the sea.'".
